hints: Notice the power is $3.7 \text{ MW}$ and you must give it in kilowatts, so focus on the two prefixes mega and kilo.
Recall that $1 \text{ MW} = 10^6 \text{ W}$ and $1 \text{ kW} = 10^3 \text{ W}$, so changing from megawatts to the smaller kilowatts must increase the number.
Check the exact SI spelling of kilowatt: kilo is lower-case $\text{k}$ and the unit watt from a person's name is upper-case $\text{W}$.
walkthrough: Start with the given power $3.7 \text{ MW}$. Mega means $10^6$, so write it in watts: $3.7 \text{ MW} = 3.7 \times 10^6 \text{ W}$.
Kilo means $10^3$, so $1 \text{ kW} = 10^3 \text{ W}$. To convert watts to kilowatts divide by $10^3$.
Set up the conversion: $\text{power in kW} = (3.7 \times 10^6)/10^3 = 3.7 \times 10^3$.
Check the unit symbol. The prefix kilo is $\text{k}$ and watt is $\text{W}$, giving $\text{kW}$. Upper-case $\text{K}$ would mean kelvin, not kilo.
So the power is $3.7 \times 10^3 \text{ kW}$. This is option C.

options.A: This divides by $1000$ instead of multiplying. $1 \text{ MW}$ is larger than $1 \text{ kW}$, so the number in $\text{kW}$ must be larger than 3.7.
options.B: This has the wrong power of ten and the wrong symbol. $\text{KW}$ is not the SI symbol for kilowatt.
options.C: $3.7 \text{ MW} = 3.7 \times 10^6 \text{ W} = 3.7 \times 10^3 \text{ kW}$ with correct lower-case k and upper-case W.
options.D: The number $3.7 \times 10^3$ is correct but $\text{KW}$ is incorrect. Kilo uses lower-case $\text{k}$ and watt uses upper-case $\text{W}$.
